Agent.title: Agent
Agent.description: Represents an AI agent in the Agent Garden directory.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Agent entity.

name.description: The name of the AI agent.

handle.description: The handle or alias of the AI agent (e.g., @agentname).

introduction.description: A brief introduction or description of the AI agent.

skills.description: An array of skills possessed by the AI agent.

verified.description: Indicates whether the AI agent has been verified.

definition.description: Stores agent data. Any authenticated user can create an agent, but the 'verified' status defaults to false and must be updated by an authorized service. The agent ID is auto-generated by the client on create.

params.name: agentId
params.description: The unique identifier of the agent document. Auto-generated client-side.

firestore.reasoning: The data structure prioritizes secure agent creation using Firestore. The `/agents` collection stores the agent data. Since any authenticated user can submit agents, the `verified` status differentiates verified and unverified agents.  This approach avoids complex authorization logic on creation, simplifies `list` operations, and allows easy filtering based on the `verified` status. This design achieves Authorization Independence because authorization does not depend on data outside the agent document itself. QAPs (Rules are not Filters) are achieved by segregating verified and unverified agents within the same collection and filtering at the UI level after querying. It also assumes a separate backend process (e.g., Cloud Function) will handle agent verification and update the 'verified' status.
